# Topology.MoveAPI.move

## `move(d::KnotGaussDiagram, type, arg::NamedTuple) -> KnotGaussDiagram`

    move(d::KnotGaussDiagram, type, arg::NamedTuple) -> KnotGaussDiagram

Apply a local Reidemeister move selected by a named argument record.

# Arguments
K1, K13 and the named-record coordinates of
[move selectors](../../specs/knot-gauss.md#move-selectors) apply.
This overload uses the keyword `move` requirements, including default
`strict=true`. Missing candidates and strict ambiguity raise `ArgumentError`;
selector and application failures propagate. Unrecognized fields are ignored.

# Returns
The `KnotGaussDiagram` returned by the corresponding keyword query.

# Guarantees
1. The output has the selected local-replacement meaning and structural verification guarantee of the keyword overload. [proved/agent: by construction]
2. The diagram and supplied record are not modified. [proved/agent: by construction]

# Not guaranteed
This does not validate all fields of an arbitrary record, canonicalize the
result, or add a topological identification beyond the keyword overload.

# Sources
cf:lib/topology.jl/docs/specs/knot-gauss.md, Move selectors — ordered selections and compatibility fields.

# Examples
```jldoctest
julia> d = KnotGaussDiagram([1,-1], [1]);

julia> move(d, "R1", (p=:delete, v=[1], e=[(2,1)], strict=true)) == KnotGaussDiagram(Int[], Int[])
true
```

Role: move

## `move(d::KnotGaussDiagram, type; param=nothing, vertices=Int[], edges=nothing, strict=true) -> KnotGaussDiagram`

    move(d::KnotGaussDiagram, type; param=nothing, vertices=Int[], edges=nothing, strict=true) -> KnotGaussDiagram

Apply a selected local Reidemeister move to a knot Gauss representation.

# Arguments
K1 and K13 in [the knot specification](../../specs/knot-gauss.md#numbered-conditions)
and the selector domain of `movable(d,type;...)` apply. The selector query's
errors propagate. An empty candidate population raises `ArgumentError`
with `No valid Reidemeister moves found`. With `strict=true`, more than one
candidate raises `ArgumentError` with `Reidemeister move is ambiguous`.
With `strict=false`, the first returned candidate is selected.
The selected application must pass `apply_reidemeister`'s structural checks;
its failures propagate. Classicality K2 is not checked.

# Returns
A `KnotGaussDiagram` carrying the local replacement of the selected witness.

# Guarantees
1. The result equals `apply_reidemeister(d,c)` for the selected witness `c`; successful return has passed the corresponding structural transition verification. [proved/agent: by construction]
2. The source diagram and selector containers are unchanged. [proved/agent: by construction]

# Not guaranteed
The result is not canonicalized. Non-strict selection does not identify a
canonical move or eliminate dependence on enumeration order. The source
comparison and general classical-knot interpretation retain the unverified
boundary in the specification; this call does not classify the knot.

# Sources
cf:lib/topology.jl/docs/specs/knot-gauss.md, Enumeration and move witnesses — local replacement and its evidence boundary.

# Examples
```jldoctest
julia> d = KnotGaussDiagram([1,-1], [1]);

julia> move(d, "R1"; param=:delete, vertices=[1], edges=[(1,2)]) == KnotGaussDiagram(Int[], Int[])
true
```

Role: move

## `move(input::HeegaardCode, witness::LCMoveWitness) -> Topology.HeegaardCodes.LCMoveResult`

    move(input::HeegaardCode, witness::LCMoveWitness) -> Topology.HeegaardCodes.LCMoveResult

Apply a supported Heegaard move witness through the common presentation interface.

# Arguments
The source-binding and supported transport conditions of
[Heegaard move witnesses](../../specs/heegaard-moves.md#comparison-and-move-witnesses)
apply. Use a witness from `movable(input,row)` for the same source and an
unmodified catalog. The selected Heegaard operation checks its supported
binding, support and transport data; failures raise `LCMoveError` with the
reason. Validation, catalog and conversion failures propagate. Hand-built
lower-level witnesses retain the specification's trusted-constructor boundary.

# Returns
An `LCMoveResult` with transformed `output`, its `inverse` witness, and a
`correspondence` dictionary, with the meanings in the
[witness specification](../../specs/heegaard-moves.md#comparison-and-move-witnesses).
Named-row LC operations remain available through `Topology.HeegaardCodes`.

# Guarantees
1. The result equals `Topology.HeegaardCodes.move(input,witness)` and has that selected operation's supported presentation meaning. [proved/agent: by construction]
2. The source presentation is not modified by this call. [proved/agent: by construction]

# Not guaranteed
General manifold preservation does not follow from a successful operation:
the relation is row-dependent and a partial-family twist can change the
manifold. The output need not be a canonical or minimal representative, nor
need an inverse recover the exact original text. Other presentation types
use their own method contracts.

# Sources
cf:lib/topology.jl/docs/specs/module-structure.md §3.1 — common move interface.
cf:lib/topology.jl/docs/specs/heegaard-moves.md §4.1 — checked witness application and relation scope.

# Examples
```jldoctest
julia> H = Topology.HeegaardCodes; lc = H.LickorishCode(1, Dict("l1" => [-1], "m1" => [1]), Dict(), Dict(), Dict(), Dict(), nothing); hc = H.resolve_hc(lc, Dict("l1" => :beta); standard=true);

julia> r = move(hc, first(movable(hc, "lc.twist.annulus"))); back = move(r.output, r.inverse);

julia> H.hc_search_state(back.output; identity=:canonical).state_id == H.hc_search_state(hc; identity=:canonical).state_id
true
```

Role: move

## `move(v::VirtualLink, candidate::MoveCandidate; boundary=nothing) -> VirtualLink`

    move(v::VirtualLink, candidate::MoveCandidate; boundary=nothing) -> VirtualLink

Return the result of an authenticated local move candidate on a VirtualLink.

# Arguments
The [candidate domain](../../specs/virtual-link-moves.md#6-candidate-contract)
and applicable [weight transport conditions](../../specs/virtual-link-moves.md#12-weight-transport)
apply. Normally obtain `candidate` from `movable(v,...)` and keep the source
unchanged. Candidate templates, orientation roles and occurrences are
compared against the current source; mismatch raises `ArgumentError` with
`move candidate does not match the current source`. Unsupported modes,
invalid PS split data, invalid boundary targets and reconstruction failures
propagate from the selected local execution. A weight or boundary check can
fail after geometric matching has succeeded.

# Returns
An independent `VirtualLink` with that candidate's local rewrite and the
selected coefficient transport. The candidate's occurrence is retained.

# Guarantees
1. The output is the result of the authenticated candidate application on an independent copy; no alternative occurrence is selected and no canonicalization is added. [proved/agent: by construction]
2. The source presentation remains unchanged on success or failure. [proved/agent: by construction]

# Not guaranteed
Matching a candidate is not a proof of a topological equivalence or of an
inverse operation. The general mathematical scope remains move- and
coefficient-dependent. An unweighted geometric candidate alone does not
certify weighted or spin transport on a different source.

# Sources
cf:lib/topology.jl/docs/specs/virtual-link-moves.md §§6, 12 and 15 — frozen local data and supported execution.

# Examples
```jldoctest
julia> v = VirtualLink(); set_data!(v; rgauss=[[-1,2,-2,3,-3,1,0]], orientation=[1,1,1]);

julia> c = only(movable(v, "MP"; param="C3", vertices=[1,2], strict=true)); target = move(v,c);

julia> count(identity, Topology.strand_cuts(target))
1
```

Role: move

## `move(v::VirtualLink, type, arg::NamedTuple) -> VirtualLink`

    move(v::VirtualLink, type, arg::NamedTuple) -> VirtualLink

Return a VirtualLink after a move selected by a named argument record.

# Arguments
The [record selectors](../../specs/virtual-link-moves.md#41-namedtuple-argument-aliases)
and keyword `move` source, placement and weight requirements apply.
`edge_occurrences` and `boundary` are recognized in addition to those aliases;
`strict` defaults to `true`. Extra fields and conflicting aliases are not
diagnosed as schema errors. Selection and execution exceptions propagate.

# Returns
A separate `VirtualLink` with the same result as the corresponding keyword
selection, including its choice among multiple candidates.

# Guarantees
1. The output carries the local rewrite and weight-transport meaning of the keyword overload. [proved/agent: by construction]
2. The source presentation and record are unchanged on success or failure. [proved/agent: by construction]

# Not guaranteed
This is not a general record-schema validator and adds no topological
certification, canonicalization or ambiguity rejection to the keyword call.

# Sources
cf:lib/topology.jl/docs/specs/virtual-link-moves.md §§4 and 12 — argument records and coefficient transport.

# Examples
```jldoctest
julia> v = VirtualLink(); set_data!(v; rgauss=[[-1,2,-2,3,-3,1,0]], orientation=[1,1,1]);

julia> target = move(v, "MP", (p="C3", v=[1,2], strict=true));

julia> count(identity, Topology.strand_cuts(target))
1
```

## `move(v::VirtualLink, type; param=nothing, vertices=Int[], edges=nothing, edge_occurrences=nothing, strict=true, boundary=nothing) -> VirtualLink`

    move(v::VirtualLink, type; param=nothing, vertices=Int[], edges=nothing, edge_occurrences=nothing, strict=true, boundary=nothing) -> VirtualLink

Return a VirtualLink after applying the selected supported local move.

# Arguments
The source, selectors and coefficient domain of `movable(v,type;...)` apply,
with [strictness](../../specs/virtual-link-moves.md#43-strictness) defaulting to
`true`. The [weight transport requirements](../../specs/virtual-link-moves.md#12-weight-transport)
and the selected execution branch's checks must also hold.
Unsupported weight families and R1/R2/R3 execution raise `ArgumentError`.
H requires a valid integer weight parameter and a weighted source.
No valid candidate raises `ArgumentError` with `No valid moves found.`.
Multiple candidates produce a warning and the first candidate is applied;
`strict` controls matching order, not rejection of every ambiguity.
Selection, local reconstruction, boundary and arithmetic failures propagate.

# Returns
A separate `VirtualLink` with the chosen local rewrite and supported weight
transport. Its raw presentation is not automatically canonicalized.

# Guarantees
1. The returned data equal the result of applying `move!` with the same request to an independent copy of the source. [proved/agent: by construction]
2. The source presentation remains unchanged, including when selection or application fails. [proved/agent: by construction]
3. The result is a rewritten presentation in the selected move family's supported domain; successful return does not broaden the family's mathematical guarantees. [proved/agent: by construction]

# Not guaranteed
The function does not certify manifold, combing or framing equivalence for
arbitrary inputs. It neither returns a move certificate nor checks a general
inverse. Use an explicit candidate when a particular occurrence matters.
Canonicality and minimality of the output are not promised.

# Sources
cf:lib/topology.jl/docs/specs/virtual-link-moves.md §§4, 8, 12 and 15 — selected local rewrite, weight domain and support boundary.

# Examples
```jldoctest
julia> v = VirtualLink(); set_data!(v; rgauss=[[-1,2,-2,3,-3,1,0]], orientation=[1,1,1]);

julia> target = move(v, "MP"; param="C3", vertices=[1,2], strict=true);

julia> count(identity, Topology.strand_cuts(target))
1
```

Role: move
